newsitem.title: USA: White House gives Herman vote of confidence.
newsitem.headline: White House gives Herman vote of confidence.

text.p: The White House Wednesday gave Labour Secretary nominee Alexis Herman a strong vote of confidence in the face of Republican criticism over her connection to a Democratic Party fundraising controversy.
"The president is certainly willing to work very hard on behalf of a nominee that he considers exceptionally well qualified," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters.

Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Tuesday Herman might have come close to violating the law in her work as a White House official. The Hatch Act bars government officials from partisan activities.

Documents released by the White House last Friday included a lengthy report by a political working group chaired by Herman, as director of the White House public liaison office, recommending ways to solidify support for President Clinton and other Democratic candidates among blacks.

The report called for creation of an African American Leadership Forum, and members would be given the opportunity to interact with administration officials and the Democratic Party's leadership through various briefings.

The report said the names of the forum's members "would be shared with the White House and invited to briefings. In addition, the DNC (Democratic National Committee) will need to ensure that contributors receive personal attention beyond personal invitations to White House affairs."
Lott said the latest development about Herman "gets awfully close to the edge of violating the Hatch Act." But he said he did not know if Herman's nomination was in jeopardy.

McCurry agreed with a reporter's suggestion that Clinton was prepared to "go to the mat" for Herman as he promised to do for Anthony Lake, whose nomination to become CIA director has been in question.

"The process is still in a very early stage, so I don't know how it could be in deep trouble," he said. "We believe that she's got a lot of intelligence, creativity and capability to bring to the position and she looks forward to the opportunity to make that case individually to senators. We're sure at the end of the day she'll successfully make the case and we will see her confirmed."

As for Lott's criticism, McCurry said: "I can't believe that the majority leader would suggest that she's disqualified from serving as secretary of labour because she attempted to encourage African Americans to participate in the political life of this nation."
